title: Kamerun
capsule: German commercial presence in Kamerun dates to 1868, when the Hamburg trading house C. Woermann established the first permanent German trading post in the Duala estuary on the Wouri River delta. This early phase (1868–1871) was purely commercial rather than colonial, with German firms—later joined by Jantzen and Thormählen—acquiring land from local Duala chiefs and developing plantation agriculture alongside British trading interests already present in the area. Formal German annexation came only in July 1884, when Gustav Nachtigal concluded protectorate treaties with the Duala chiefs and hoisted the German flag, transforming the commercial beachhead into the colony of Kamerun.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The 1868–1871 attestation reflects German commercial rather than territorial control; no formal boundaries existed, and the footprint was limited to trading posts on the Wouri estuary.
